Orchestrator close verification — all three ACs re-proven on this host at close time, not inferred
from the merge.

Fix merged as `98d4ab96325d` ("Fix mechanism-delta test import under bare pytest").

## AC1 — both halves, run just now

```
$ pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py::test_a_marker_in_a_new_gate_scripts_head_admits_it -q
1 passed in 1.82s                        <- the BARE console script, the reported reproduction

$ python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q
32 passed in 104.15s                     <- and the module still green under -m
```

Both invocation modes pass, which is the point: the bug was that only ONE of them worked.

## AC2 — the import is explicit, derived from `__file__`

`tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py:42-43` inserts `_SCRIPTS_DIR` on `sys.path` at module import,
and `:29` derives it from `Path(__file__).resolve()`. The comment at `:36-38` records the
non-obvious part — it is the `scripts/` directory, NOT the repository root — so the next reader
does not "fix" it back to the root. No reliance on collection order remains, and the reported
`ModuleNotFoundError` does not appear in either run above.

## AC3 — the isolation property is enforced, not incidental

`test_the_reported_selection_passes_standalone` at `:424`, carrying the marker
`allow_unharnessed_subprocess("spawns the BARE pytest console script; the child's own sys.path IS
the thing under test")`. That is the correct shape: an in-process assertion could not have caught
this, because the parent's `sys.path` is exactly what was masking the defect.

## Close class

`preexisting`. The defect was latent from when the module was written — the import happened to
resolve because some other collected test had already put `scripts/` on `sys.path`. Nothing
regressed; a narrower selection simply stopped supplying the accident. Recording it that way
matters, because "it only fails in a narrow selection" is the signature of an incidental
dependency, not of a flake, and treating it as a flake would have meant retrying it forever.
